VF EMPIRE · AI TRAINING CENTRE

Models come in raw. They leave as systems.

The VF AI Training Centre is a working centre on the same floor where VF builds its own machines. Open-source models come in raw and leave as complete systems: engines fitted, harnesses tuned, dashboards live. Four lanes, one discipline, and the first intake is forming now.

First intake forming Four lanes Malta, EU
Register interest See the four lanes
WHAT IT IS

A working centre.
The same floor, the same method.

The VF centre teaches the machine around the model: how an open model is installed, steered, harnessed, gated and put on a dashboard so that it does real work on hardware the owner controls. That is the method behind every system on the build slate and the software thesis that produced it.

The floor.

The centre runs where VF runs: more than 200 specialised agents and more than 60 supervised process lanes, local-first on owned hardware. You learn on the machines that build the products.

The method.

The Helmsman engine, the harness stack and the command dashboards, taught as one discipline. Swap the model, keep the machine.

The proof.

S◉LOCK, the first complete system off the line, and VF Mail, already serving inboxes on VF metal. Every lane in the centre shipped inside them first.

THE FLOOR
THE FOUR LANES

Fit. Harness. Control.
Then make it earn its keep.

Each lane maps to one part of a VF system. Together they cover the whole path from a raw model to a machine an owner can run.

LANE 01
Open-model fitting.

Installing, tuning and steering frontier-class open models on owned metal, the way Helmsman does it on the VF floor: routing work across models, curating them like instruments, keeping the cloud optional.

LANE 02
Harness engineering.

Building the frame that turns a raw model into a worker: process supervision, self-heal loops, project memory and evidence discipline. Every lane ends in a gate; nothing ships on a model's word alone.

LANE 03
Dashboard and control design.

Designing the command surfaces: fleets, lanes, costs and outcomes on one pane of glass. If it runs, it is visible; if it drifts, it pages. The surfaces every commissioned system is handed over with.

LANE 04
Utilisation labs.

VF research measures how much real, gated, verified work one model can do per day. The labs put you on that measurement: batching, routing, tool discipline, context economy. The benchmark is finished work.

WHO IT IS FOR

Operators, deployers,
and the people who join the floor.

The Terms of Service state the purpose in one line: the centre's programmes are designed to advance the AI literacy of the people who operate, deploy and are affected by AI systems, as Article 4 of the EU AI Act asks.

Teams that commission a system

Every VF handover includes dashboards, documentation and training. The centre is where that training lives, so the people who will run the machine learn it on the floor that built it. Start at commission a system.

Engineers running open models

Anyone already running open models who wants gated, verified work from them. Lanes 01, 02 and 04 are built for this.

Designers of control surfaces

Interface, motion and industrial designers who want their work on a live dashboard. Lane 03, and the open invitation to propose an integration.

People joining the floor

The centre is one route onto the VF operating floor. Applications go to careers@vfempire.com and are answered within 3 business days; see careers.

Manufacturers under the CRA

Teams that need the security discipline behind the security posture in-house, alongside the fixed-fee CRA Readiness Audit.

INTAKE

First intake forming.
Dates and fees by email.

The first intake is forming now. VF publishes no date or fee until it is fixed; intake dates and fees go out by email to everyone who has registered interest.

To register interest, write to info@vfempire.com with the subject "Training Centre", the lane you want and whether you come as an individual or a team. The desk replies within the hour. To apply for a place on the floor through the centre, write to careers@vfempire.com; the reply comes within 3 business days.

Training programmes are governed by a separate written agreement, as section 6 of the Terms sets out. An email registers interest and creates no obligation on either side.

QUESTIONS

Asked.
Answered.

What is the VF AI Training Centre?

A working centre on the floor where VF Empire builds its own machines. Open-source models come in raw and leave as complete systems: engines fitted, harnesses tuned, dashboards live. It teaches the method behind every VF system, in four lanes: open-model fitting, harness engineering, dashboard and control design, and utilisation labs. The first intake is forming now.

When does the first intake start and what does it cost?

The first intake is forming and no date or fee is published yet. VF sends intake dates and fees by email to everyone who has registered interest, before anything is announced publicly. Register by writing to info@vfempire.com with the subject "Training Centre"; the desk replies within the hour and keeps you on the list.

Who should attend the AI Training Centre?

Teams that commission a VF system and will run it, engineers who already run open models and want gated, verified work from them, designers of control surfaces, manufacturers who need the security discipline in-house, and people who want to join the VF floor. The programmes advance the AI literacy of operators and deployers, as Article 4 of the EU AI Act asks.

Where is the AI Training Centre?

On the VF floor, the same floor where VF runs its own agents and lanes local-first on hardware it owns. VF Empire Corp Ltd is registered in Malta, in the European Union, as C 94160, with its office in Għajnsielem, Gozo; the about page has the full company record.

Is the Training Centre a route to working at VF?

Yes. The centre is one route onto the operating floor; direct application is the other. Both go through careers@vfempire.com, where our AI does the first-pass triage, a person reviews the shortlist weekly and you get a reply within 3 business days. The careers page explains the process and states that no roles are open today.
